tests.title: parses deblock_options with native defaults, shorthand order, filter constants, integer expressions and last-wins keys
declares the native pix_fmts in declared order and refuses edges within the kernel reach of the right plane border
ports the weak and strong kernels, the block loop with its border skips and the vertical stop at a skipped row
rejects unsupported layouts, budgets, malformed storage, invalid settings and cancellation explicitly
plans deblock on every path with edge-reach refusals and refuses enable= and runtime commands
runs against the sandbox reference build of commit 946fcce0 configured with --disable-x86asm
matches native deblock through the linear, frame graph and replay APIs across formats, sizes, patterns and options
matches native deblock rawvideo and framecrc bytes on every flagged CLI path with and without -ss/-t
stops each vertical edge at its first skipped row like native on every CLI path
agrees with native under default filter threads and -filter_threads 1
fails like native for out-of-range and unknown deblock options before opening outputs on every path
negotiates every accepted source as native does and refuses picks without storage before output on every path

details: 1446 native rawvideo outputs matched byte for byte by compileVideoFilterChain, compileVideoFilterGraph and createReplayVideoExecution (4338 path comparisons): 6 formats x 8 sizes x 3 patterns x 14 option sets, 3 frames; 570 edge-reach cases refused on all three APIs

1980 CLI rawvideo/framecrc outputs matched on linear, graph, stream, actor (timed producer) and timed (pull), with and without input -ss 0.04 / output -t 0.05; 1020 edge-reach refusals with no output opened
10 vertical-stop quirk comparisons (weak/strong x 5 CLI paths)
9 thread cases: native default threads == -filter_threads 1 == linear plan
45 option-error refusals (9 errors x 5 paths) with native diagnostics checked

unsupported: enable= timeline, runtime commands (native process_command) and generic filter options
expression-valued and hexadecimal float thresholds (alpha/beta/gamma/delta accept decimal literals only)
edges within kernel reach of a selected plane's right border: width > block with width % block == 1 (weak) or in 1..2 (strong); native reads and writes past the row
high-bit-depth formats and native formats without storage here (yuva444p, yuva422p, yuv440p, yuv411p, yuv410p, yuvj440p, yuvj411p, gbrap): refused by name when negotiated
no dedicated H.264/MP4 framecrc comparison (size unchanged)

proposedContracts.scope: gray/yuv420p/yuv422p/yuv444p/yuva420p/gbrp, 8 sizes incl. 16x16 and 33x17, noise/blocky/ramp, weak/strong, block 4..512, thresholds 0..1, plane masks, rawvideo, edge-reach refusals

proposedContracts.scope: CLI rawvideo and framecrc, with and without -ss/-t, edge-reach refusals before output

proposedContracts.name: stops each vertical edge at its first skipped row like native on every CLI path
agrees with native under default filter threads and -filter_threads 1
fails like native for out-of-range and unknown deblock options before opening outputs on every path
proposedContracts.scope: option range, name and arity errors with no output opened

proposedContracts.name: negotiates every accepted source as native does and refuses picks without storage before output on every path
proposedContracts.scope: per-source negotiation over the 17 shared sources; gbrap picks refused by name

notes: Native quirk ported exactly: deblockv*_weak/strong advance dst at the end of the loop body, which the skip branch's continue jumps over, so each vertical edge segment stops at its first skipped row. Found by a C replica of the native loop that matched native byte for byte.
Threshold conversion: ath..dth = trunc(fround(fround(value) * 255)), done once at parse time; default alpha 0.098 gives 24.
No linux-gated cases: every case is integer after the one IEEE single-precision threshold conversion.

Setup: bootstrap script refused Node 22 ('Node.js 24+ is required') and installing Node 24 was not permitted in the sandbox, so the spec fallback was used with Node v22.23.5: git submodule update 105s, npm ci 9s, npm run reference:build 202s. Baseline typecheck+lint+boundaries plus registry unit test: 77s (all passed, 8 registry tests).
Final checks: unit 5/5 and registry 8/8 passed; differential 7/7 passed in about 31s with --maxWorkers=1; typecheck, lint and boundaries clean.
